provider: PubMed Central Open Access Subset (pmc-oa-opendata on S3)
category: open-access full-text research corpus (world-readable S3 bucket)

free_tier.stated: 'PMC makes the datasets described below freely accessible on Amazon Web Services (AWS), without charge, through either an HTTPS or S3 URL, and without any log-in requirement for retrieval.' The README reports 'roughly 8 million PMC article versions'.
free_tier.notes: The bucket is s3://pmc-oa-opendata in us-east-1; the AWS Open Data Sponsorship Program covers the transfer.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: one object per article file (JATS XML, plain text, PDF, media). A full-text XML measured here was 109,974 bytes.

retention.stated: articles stay while their licence holds; 'If a version is removed from the S3 bucket, its prefix and all associated files are deleted from the bucket with no explicit notification. Inventory reconciliation is the only supported way to detect removals.' The inventory is regenerated daily and kept 30 days.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered: NLM pays through the AWS Open Data Sponsorship Program. 'No charges, usage fees or royalties are paid to NLM for these data.' Both https://pmc-oa-opendata.s3.amazonaws.com/<prefix>/<file> and s3:// with --no-sign-request work.

interface_detail: S3 REST and HTTPS on the same bucket. aws s3 cp --no-sign-request s3://pmc-oa-opendata/<PMCID>.<version>/<PMCID>.<version>.xml, or curl the equivalent https URL. S3 Inventory under inventory-reports/ gives a daily CSV manifest.
tooling: AWS CLI with --no-sign-request, curl, boto3 unsigned, rclone (S3 remote with anonymous access). Any of them reaches the bucket; nothing needs an account.
chaining: The full-text corpus that pairs with Europe PMC's metadata index: harvest PMID/PMCID lists from Europe PMC or the PMC inventory, then pull the XML here. Licences per article decide what a derivative may redistribute.

limits.value: no request cap is published for the S3 bucket; the article-dataset page restricts automated retrieval to the Cloud Service, OAI-PMH, E-utilities and BioC API
one object per article file; measured full-text XML is 109,974 bytes, so a 1 TiB pull is roughly 10 million objects

limits_note: The 2026-08-24 change removed the legacy FTP and cloud dataset files and left the S3 bucket as the distribution path.
binding_note: Nothing fails at 1 TiB/month: the whole corpus is smaller than that. At the measured 109,974 bytes per article version, 8 million versions is about 880 GB of XML before PDFs and media - arithmetic from the two published numbers, not a measurement of the bucket.

identity_cost.detail: 'without any log-in requirement for retrieval'; an unsigned HTTPS GET for a full-text XML returned 200 here. No Earthdata-style account, no API key.

reliability_note: Removed articles vanish with no notification; the inventory lags the bucket by up to a day, so a manifest-driven sync always races deletions.
confidence_note: Two objects were fetched anonymously and hashed here (README.txt 14,524 bytes; one full-text XML 109,974 bytes) and the bucket's accept-ranges is byte. What is not measured is aggregate throughput at 1 and 8 connections.

evidence.proved: world-readable bucket s3://pmc-oa-opendata, 'without any log-in requirement for retrieval', --no-sign-request, and the removal-without-notification clause
'roughly 8 million PMC article versions' and the <PMCID>.<version>/ object layout
'All legacy PMC Article Dataset files on the FTP and Cloud Services were removed the week of August 24, 2026' - the bulk path changed in 2026
only the Cloud Service, OAI-PMH, E-Utilities and BioC API may be used for automated retrieval of PMC content

notes: This is the strongest no-account research corpus: 8 million article versions, no login, S3 range reads, a daily inventory. The 2026-08-24 distribution change is the reason a record written before it would name FTP paths that no longer exist.
